Suppose $Y$ is a continuous random variable. We wish to conduct a chi-square goodness-of-fit test at the $5%$ significance level with the following null and alternative hypotheses:

- $H_{0}$: $Y∼N(5, σ^{2})$
- $H_{1}$: $Y≁N(5, σ^{2})$

where the variance $σ^{2}$ is unknown.

A random sample is carried out, and the sample data is shown below.

| Observations $(y_{i})$ | Frequency $(O_{i})$ |
| --- | ---: |
| $0 \le y_{i} < 2$ | $12$ |
| $2 \le y_{i} < 4$ | $11$ |
| $4 \le y_{i} < 6$ | $9$ |
| $6 \le y_{i} < 8$ | $15$ |
| $8 \le y_{i} < 10$ | $8$ |

Find an estimate for the variance $σ^{2}$, rounded to one decimal place.

Our estimate for $σ^{2}$ is {{field-1}}.

> A scientific calculator is required to answer this question.

Suppose $Y$ is a continuous random variable. We wish to conduct a chi-square goodness-of-fit test at the $1%$ significance level with the following null and alternative hypotheses:

- $H_{0}$: $Y∼N(μ, (\sqrt{11})^{2})$
- $H_{1}$: $Y≁N(μ, (\sqrt{11})^{2})$

where the mean $μ$ is unknown.

A random sample is carried out, and the sample data is shown below.

| Observations $(y_{i})$ | Frequency $(O_{i})$ |
| --- | ---: |
| $0 \le y_{i} < 3$ | $11$ |
| $3 \le y_{i} < 6$ | $16$ |
| $6 \le y_{i} < 9$ | $15$ |
| $9 \le y_{i} < 12$ | $18$ |

Find an estimate for the mean $μ$.

Our estimate for $μ$ is {{field-1}}.
